Under the standard LINE formulation, the model does not use Radial Basis Function (RBF) Support Vector Machines, Sequential Minimal Optimization (SMO), or dual Lagrange multipliers. LINE is a graph embedding method that learns a mapping function from vertices to low-dimensional vector space by optimizing first-order and second-order proximity objectives with stochastic gradient-based methods. Therefore, there is no LINE-specific set of SVM KKT conditions to detail.

If one instead considers the hypothetical assumption in your query—namely, replacing LINE's usual objective with an RBF SVM trained by SMO—then the relevant Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions would be the standard soft-margin SVM conditions. For training examples (x_i, y_i) with y_i in {−1, +1}, primal feasibility requires y_i (w^T φ(x_i) + b) ≥ 1 − ξ_i and ξ_i ≥ 0. Dual feasibility requires 0 ≤ α_i ≤ C for each Lagrange multiplier α_i. Complementary slackness requires α_i [y_i (w^T φ(x_i) + b) − 1 + ξ_i] = 0 and (C − α_i) ξ_i = 0. Stationarity gives w = Σ_i α_i y_i φ(x_i) and Σ_i α_i y_i = 0. For an RBF kernel, the decision function is f(x) = Σ_i α_i y_i K(x_i, x) + b with K(x_i, x) = exp(−γ ||x_i − x||^2).

Interpreting these conditions in the embedding context, each training point would be a node embedding or node-pair feature vector, and the learned classifier would separate classes in the induced feature space. However, this is not how LINE is originally defined, so these KKT conditions are only applicable to the hypothetical SVM replacement, not to LINE itself.
